questions.question:
Select the interjection in the following sentence:
"Goodness, I had no idea the presentation was due this morning."

options.text: Goodness
idea
presentation
morning

questions.question:
What type of interjection is used in the following sentence?
"Shh! The baby has just fallen asleep."

options.text: Emotive
Cognitive
Agreement
Volitive

questions.question: Identify the sentence that uses a word as a secondary interjection rather than its typical part of speech.

options.text: "Ouch! That injection was more painful than I expected."
"Wow! The view from the summit was unlike anything I had ever seen."
"Now, let us think this through before we make a decision we might regret."
"Yikes! I completely forgot to submit the assignment before the deadline."

questions.question: Which of the following interjections best demonstrates the use of regional slang in informal spoken English?

options.text: "Oh! You startled me."
"Wow! That was unexpected."
"Blimey! I did not see that coming at all."
"Ah! Now I understand what you meant."

questions.question:
Identify the modifier in the following sentence:
"The quietly spoken teacher explained the concept with remarkable patience."

options.text: teacher
quietly spoken
concept
patience

questions.question: Which of the following sentences contains a misplaced modifier?

options.text: Running through the park, she spotted a rare butterfly near the pond.
He returned the book to the library with a torn cover.
Balanced carefully on the edge, the vase caught everyone's attention.
Covered in mud, the children rushed through the back door after the game.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences contains a dangling modifier?

options.text: Having studied all night, Maya felt confident going into the examination.
Exhausted after the long hike, the team set up camp near the river.
Laughing loudly at the joke, the children barely noticed the teacher enter.
Determined to meet the deadline, the project was completed two days early.

questions.question:
Which of the following correctly rewrites this sentence to fix the misplaced modifier?
"She found a note under the door from her neighbour."

options.text: Under the door, the note from her neighbour was found by her.
She found a note from her neighbour under the door.
Her neighbour's note was found by her under the door.
She found under the door a note from her neighbour.

questions.question: A student is preparing for a grammar test and asks her teacher to help her identify which of the following is a correctly formed passive voice sentence.

options.text: The documents sent to the wrong department by the intern last Tuesday.
The bridge was constructed over a period of five years by a team of engineers.
The contestants were cheer by the crowd throughout the entire performance.
The manager was approve the revised budget before the deadline.

questions.question: A teacher gives four sentences and says three share the same voice. One is the odd one out. Which sentence does NOT belong with the others?

options.text: The letter was delivered to the wrong address by the courier.
The finalist presented her design to the panel of judges.
The garden was maintained by a team of volunteers throughout the year.
The new policy was announced by the principal at the start of term.

questions.question:
A teacher writes this sentence on the board:
"The scientists discovered a new species in the remote rainforest."
She asks two students to convert it into passive voice.
Marco writes: "A new species was discovered in the remote rainforest by the scientists."
Leila writes: "A new species was discover in the remote rainforest by the scientists."
Which student got it right?

options.text: Only Marco
Only Leila
Both Marco and Leila
Neither Marco nor Leila

questions.question:
A student attempts to convert the following passive sentence into active voice:
"The annual prize was awarded to the winner by them."
The student writes: "Them awarded the annual prize to the winner."
Which of the following is the correctly rewritten version?

options.text: Them awarded the annual prize to the winner.
The annual prize awarded to the winner by them.
They awarded the annual prize to the winner.
They were awarding the annual prize to the winner.

questions.question: A student is writing a story and shows her teacher four sentences. Which one is correctly punctuated?

options.text: "I can't believe we won the match" she said.
"I can't believe we won the match." she said.
"I can't believe we won the match," she said.
"I can't believe we won the match", she said.

questions.question: A teacher gives four sentences and says three share the same form. One is the odd one out. Which sentence does NOT belong with the others?

options.text: She mentioned that she had already spoken to the head of department.
They confirmed that the results would be published by the end of the week.
"Nobody told me the meeting had been moved," he said quietly.
He explained that the train had been delayed due to bad weather.

questions.question:
A teacher writes this sentence on the board:
"We are leaving for the trip tomorrow morning," said the coach.
She asks the class to fill in the blank in the indirect version:
The coach said that they _______ for the trip the following morning.

options.text: are leaving
were leaving
have been leaving
will be leaving

questions.question:
A student converts the following sentence into indirect speech:
"We have already submitted our report," said the managers.
The student writes: We said that we had already submitted our report.
Which option correctly rewrites it?

options.text: The managers said that we had already submitted our report.
The managers said that they have already submitted their report.
The managers said that they had already submitted their report.
The managers said that them had already submitted their report.

questions.question: Which of the following is an opinion?

options.text: The Great Wall of China stretches over twenty-one thousand kilometres in total length.
The human heart beats approximately seventy times per minute at rest.
Leonardo da Vinci was born in Italy in the year 1452.
Italian cuisine is undoubtedly the finest in the world and no other tradition can match it.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fact?

options.text: The works of Shakespeare are far too difficult for students under the age of sixteen to appreciate.
Space exploration is a wasteful use of public funding that benefits very few people.
The Apollo 11 mission successfully landed on the Moon on the 20th of July, 1969.
History is the most important subject in any school curriculum because it teaches us who we are.

questions.question:
A teacher writes the following sentence on the board:
"Given the state of the economy, the government will almost certainly raise taxes before the end of the year."
She then asks why this is an opinion and not a fact.

options.text: Because it is about the government, and statements about political decisions are always opinions
Because it is a prediction about the future that cannot be proven true at the moment it is stated, even if supported by current evidence
Because it does not name a specific country or a specific tax, making it too vague to qualify as a fact
Because the word "almost" signals that the writer is not completely certain, which automatically makes the statement an opinion

questions.question:
Read the following sentence:
"The River Thames, which runs through London, is the most historically significant waterway in England."
Which part of the sentence is a fact and which part is an opinion?

options.text: "Runs through London" is the opinion and "most historically significant waterway" is the fact
Both parts are facts because they both describe the River Thames
"Runs through London" is the fact and "most historically significant waterway in England" is the opinion
Both parts are opinions because rivers change course and "significant" cannot be defined precisely
